info.title: CF Meet Messaging API
info.description: HTTP surface of services/messaging: GET /health, /ready, /openapi.json (public, no data); the customer API under /v1/messaging and /v1/conversations (CF Meet API credential verified by Platform Access — afresh for every mutation; a verified acting principal; 503 when Platform Access is unreachable — fail closed; client tokens are accepted only on the member operations whose security lists clientToken (elsewhere 401 CLIENT_TOKENS_NOT_ENABLED); the device-direct realtime routes /v1/realtime/tickets (client token) and /v1/realtime (WebSocket, single-use ticket) authenticate themselves). /internal/v1/** is service-authenticated and exposes no operation yet. Request bodies are limited to 512 KiB. 1.13.0: GET /v1/conversations/{conversationId}/messages/{messageId}/thread (thread summary); pin expiry; conversation retentionSeconds / expiryGraceSeconds. Member roles, invitations (POST .../invitation/accept|decline, GET /v1/messaging/invitations). 1.14.0: existing DIRECT creation accepts counterpartCfMeetId, and membership addition accepts cfMeetId, as exclusive alternatives to principal UUIDs. Personal scope only; server-authenticated actor, purpose-bound resolution and authoritative policy checks; no new endpoints. 1.16.0: x-cfmeet-required-scope (the API Gateway scope pre-check) on the 92 credential operations whose handler requires exactly one registry scope (including the Section 13 session-device issue / revoke: messages.read / messages.send); GET /v1/conversations, GET /v1/conversations/{id} and GET/DELETE …/members keep a per-request choice (messages.read with an acting principal, else conversations.manage) and stay upstream-checked (Section 15, PLT-011). 1.17.0: GET /v1/messaging/push/configuration (push platforms of the deployment and the Web Push application-server key; messages.read). 1.20.0 (CF Meet Platform Build, ADR 0062 / 0063): the userToken security scheme (Authorization: Bearer cfut_..., a CF Meet user token verified by Platform Access); POST /v1/messaging/user-sessions exchanges it for a MANAGED-only partner session device and client token (EXTERNAL environments, msg grant; MESSAGING_PARTNER_SESSION_DEVICES_ENABLED); PUT / DELETE /v1/messaging/user-push-registrations/{installationId} (partner push registrations synchronised to the Notification Service; MESSAGING_PARTNER_PUSH_ENABLED). A partner session device's client token reaches only a closed MANAGED-only allowlist of the clientToken member operations (conversations and members read; messages list / get / send / edit / delete; reactions; read cursor; unread; events; attachments create / finalize / get / download grants; conversation search; reports): every other operation answers 401 CLIENT_TOKENS_NOT_ENABLED / PARTNER_ROUTE_NOT_ALLOWED and a PRIVATE_E2EE conversation answers 404. Realtime tickets and WebSocket upgrades of partner session devices also accept the environment's allowed websites (Platform Access) as Origin. 1.21.0 (CF Meet Apps, ADR 0064; MESSAGING_APPS_ENABLED): the oauthAccessToken security scheme (Authorization: Bearer cfoa_… OAuth access token or cfob_… bot token of a CF Meet App, verified by Platform Access) on the operations an app may use: conversations and members (read), messages (list, get, send, edit, delete), reactions, read cursor, unread, events, attachments (create, finalize, get, download grants), conversation search, search across the principal's MANAGED conversations, reports and invitation accept / decline. An OAuth credential acts only as the one principal it is restricted to (the granting user or the app's organization bot; CF-Acting-Principal may only repeat it, else 403 PRINCIPAL_NOT_AUTHORIZED / ACTING_PRINCIPAL_MISMATCH), sees MANAGED conversations only (PRIVATE_E2EE answers 404 and is absent from lists and search counts), and every other operation answers 403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE / OAUTH_ROUTE_NOT_ALLOWED (with the flag off every operation answers 403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE / OAUTH_NOT_ENABLED). Messages an app sent carry viaApplicationId. A CF Meet App's bot (BOT_OR_SERVICE, reference app:<appId>) is a member of MANAGED conversations only (403 PRINCIPAL_NOT_AUTHORIZED / APP_BOT_MANAGED_ONLY). 1.22.0: MLS self-join: submitMlsCommit accepts groupInfo (the GroupInfo of the new epoch) and external commits of the acting principal's own ACTIVE device; getMlsGroupState returns the current epoch's groupInfo; the device directory shows keyPackagesAvailable for the acting principal's own devices; claimKeyPackages can be limited to deviceIds. 1.23.0 (chat controls): PUT /v1/conversations/{conversationId}/inbox-settings (F1: the member's own archive / pin, at most three pins; returned in the inbox summary); PRIVATE_E2EE sends accept mentionedPrincipalIds (B3, ids only); PATCH retentionSeconds may lengthen or turn off disappearing messages (null) within the policy, by a chat admin (B4). 1.24.0 (chat organization and polls): favourite on PUT /v1/conversations/{conversationId}/inbox-settings and in the inbox summary (WhatsApp Favourites); the member's own chat lists GET / POST /v1/messaging/chat-lists, PATCH / DELETE /v1/messaging/chat-lists/{listId}, PUT / DELETE /v1/messaging/chat-lists/{listId}/conversations/{conversationId} (at most 20 lists of 500 conversations; never visible to anyone else; removing an item never touches the conversation); MANAGED polls (send with poll; PUT .../messages/{messageId}/poll/vote, POST .../messages/{messageId}/poll/close; events messaging.poll.voted / closed carry the current tally); a MANAGED group's description (create / PATCH description) and group photo (avatarRef attachment:<attachmentId>); a group admin may change title, avatarRef and description. 1.25.0 (ADR 0069): Status (24-hour statuses with server-enforced audience snapshots of mutual contacts, close friends and named lists, mutes, rings, viewers, reactions, replies, forwards and reshares) and Channels under /v1/messaging/status and /v1/messaging/channels, with resumable part uploads to protected object storage. Status content is stored server-side (not end-to-end encrypted). 1.26.0: PATCH /v1/messaging/status/{statusId} (the author's Allow sharing per status). 1.27.0 (ADR 0071): Events under /v1/messaging/events: personal and conversation events (organization and community scopes reserved), co-organizers, invitations, RSVP with counts, per-person reminders, server-side recurrence (RRULE subset in the event time zone), cancellation, ICS export as JSON, cover photos in the ADR 0069 media store and a link to a CF Meet meeting (no scheduling in Messaging). Event text is stored server-side (not end-to-end encrypted). 1.28.0 (ADR 0072): Channels complete under /v1/messaging/channels: unique handles, PUBLIC / PRIVATE channels, invite links, admins and ownership transfer, mute, discovery filters / sort / cursor, suggestions, handle lookup, every post kind with polls, scheduled posts, pins, edits, stars, views and forwards, reports, verification applications (decided only by HQ through the admin bridge), moderation history, audit log and analytics. 1.29.0 (ADR 0073): Communities under /v1/messaging/communities (groups under one structure with an Announcements group, linked or created groups with OPEN / RESTRICTED access, invitations, revocable invite links, join requests, bans, roles OWNER / ADMIN / MEMBER and group admins, chat-list preference); every community resource answers 404 to non-members; joining a group opens a new history window (nothing earlier is visible). 1.30.0 (ADR 0074): GET /v1/messaging/status/{statusId}/replies (the author's private replies of a live status); Status.replyCount, StatusViewer.reactedAt and the rings' mentionedMe flags.

post.description: Scope messages.send, acting member. Commits the message with the next canonical sequence and its durable event in one transaction (no realtime publish before commit). PRIVATE_E2EE: the PUBLIC MLS framing must name this group, an application message and the group's current epoch (EPOCH_MISMATCH otherwise; MLS_REKEY_REQUIRED while removals are pending). Retries with the same clientMessageId and bytes replay (200). PRIVATE_E2EE application content must use MLS PrivateMessage wire format; public application frames are rejected with 422 CONTENT_REJECTED / APPLICATION_MUST_BE_PRIVATE. Public handshake commits remain supported. The server checks public framing and authenticated device authorization, not AEAD authenticity; receiving clients verify ciphertext before accepting content. S13: SEND_RESTRICTED / ANNOUNCEMENT_ONLY for a non-admin member of an announcement-only conversation. S2: PRIVATE_E2EE sends may carry frankingCommitment (verifiable reports). 1.24.0: MANAGED poll — poll (2-12 options; text is the question, 1-300 characters); refused for PRIVATE_E2EE (POLL_MANAGED_ONLY).

post.description: Scope messages.send, acting member. The MLS Delivery Service accepts exactly one commit per epoch (the first; others EPOCH_MISMATCH), stores it as an MLS_COMMIT message in the canonical sequence and the Welcome per welcomed device (ACTIVE devices of ACTIVE members only). A commit may carry the GroupInfo of the epoch it creates (stored and served by getMlsGroupState while current). An external commit (sender new_member_commit) is the acting principal's own ACTIVE device joining by itself, without any other member online: never with welcome or removedDeviceIds (422 EXTERNAL_COMMIT_CANNOT_WELCOME_OR_REMOVE), never while a removal of a device still in the tree is pending (409 MLS_REKEY_REQUIRED, reason REMOVALS_PENDING_BEFORE_JOIN).

customerCredential.description: A CF Meet API credential, verified by Platform Access (never by Messaging).

userToken.description: A CF Meet user token (`cfut_<sbx|test|live>_<JWS>`, at most 2048 bytes) minted by the partner's server for one partner user (ADR 0062). Messaging never verifies it itself: Platform Access does, live (a positive answer is reused at most 30 s). Accepted only by the operations that list it.

clientToken.name: Authorization
clientToken.description: CF-Client-Token <Messaging Client Access Token> (device-direct, §105). Accepted by POST /v1/realtime/tickets and, as an alternative to customerCredential, by the member operations that list it: the token's session (device ACTIVE, session ACTIVE and unexpired, principal ACTIVE) is the caller, acting only for its own principal and own device (CF-Acting-Principal may only repeat it). Every other operation answers 401 CLIENT_TOKENS_NOT_ENABLED.

realtimeTicket.name: Sec-WebSocket-Protocol
realtimeTicket.description: `cfmeet.messaging.v1, cfmeet.ticket.<ticket>`: the single-use ticket travels as a subprotocol entry; the server answers `cfmeet.messaging.v1` only.

oauthAccessToken.description: A CF Meet App's OAuth access token (`cfoa_…`, acting for the granting CF Meet user) or bot token (`cfob_…`, acting as the app's organization bot), verified live by Platform Access (never by Messaging) — ADR 0064, MESSAGING_APPS_ENABLED. The credential acts only as the single principal it is restricted to, sees MANAGED conversations only (a PRIVATE_E2EE conversation is 404) and is accepted only by the operations that list it; elsewhere 403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE / OAUTH_ROUTE_NOT_ALLOWED.
